brief.outcome: Get the garlic press back to 55 or more units a day on Amazon US within six weeks of approval, by finding out why it fell off page one and fixing the causes, with Sponsored Products spend kept at or under $120 a day.

ambition.goal_beyond: The garlic press stays on page one and selling steadily, and a change to the listing can no longer quietly halve sales for three weeks before anyone notices.
rungs: Find what pushed the listing off page one and fix the biggest cause
Find the decisions behind the drop (the image change, the review, the ad set-up) by changing one thing at a time, and win back 55+ units a day
Keep it true: a weekly check of units, unit session percentage, ad cost per unit and search position that flags a slide inside a week, not three
ambition.judge: Seller Central business report units per day and unit session percentage for the same ASIN, compared with the three weeks before the drop; plus search position for 'garlic press' checked by the owner in a logged-out browser window

Learnings and a weekly watch rule saved

answers.question: What is the product, and where did it rank?
answers.answer: Kitchen gadget brand, garlic press on Amazon US; ranked around position 4 for 'garlic press', now on page two

answers.question: How big is the drop and where does the number come from?
answers.answer: Daily units from about 60 to 30 over three weeks (Seller Central business report, reported by the owner)

answers.question: What changed around the drop?
answers.answer: Rating 4.4 from 2,100 reviews; a 1-star review with photos appeared about a month ago; the main image was changed two weeks before the drop

answers.question: Ad spend and access?
answers.answer: Sponsored Products $90 a day; Seller Central CSV exports only; the owner can make listing changes

answers.question: Target, deadline, limits?
answers.answer: 55 or more units a day within six weeks, ad spend not above $120 a day, data kept in the project, the owner decides

research.approach: Practitioners split a sales drop before they explain it: they put daily sessions, unit session percentage (units divided by sessions) and Buy Box share side by side and ask whether fewer people arrived or fewer arrived people bought. Amazon does not publish how organic rank is computed, so they treat rank as a result of sales and conversion and read it from their own numbers rather than from blog rules of thumb. They line up every change on a dated log (image, price, review, bids, stock), read the ad reports for waste and cost rise, fix one thing at a time, and test image changes against the old one before keeping them.

steps.name: Build the dated timeline and pull the raw reports
steps.why: A drop only has a cause if it can be lined up with a dated change; the daily reports are the raw material, not the owner's summary.

steps.name: Split the drop into visits, buying rate and offer health
steps.why: Fewer sessions, a lower unit session percentage and a lost Buy Box need different fixes.

steps.name: Read the ad reports for waste and cost rise
steps.why: The ads carry about a third of the visits and rank follows sales; wasted spend and rising cost per click show up in the search term and placement reports.

steps.name: Test each cause against the numbers
steps.why: The image, the review, the ads, competitors and season can all act together; keep competing explanations until the numbers separate them.

steps.name: Change one thing at a time and test image changes against the old image
steps.why: Two changes at once make the result unreadable; an image test against the old one shows whether the change cost clicks.

steps.name: Read weekly against the target and the ceiling
steps.why: Early checks at least twice a week and a weekly readout catch a slide or a spend breach before it costs weeks.

pitfalls.text: Treating blog 'A10' weightings as fact; Amazon does not publish how rank is computed, so read rank from your own sales and conversion data.
Raising ad spend to buy rank back before the conversion problem is found, which wastes money if the page converts worse than before.
Negating or pausing search terms on too few clicks.
Changing the image, title and ads in the same week, so nobody can say which change helped.

stages.name: Pin down the drop
stages.goal: Turn the owner's words into a measured problem, a target, limits and the data we can reach. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Line up the daily numbers and the change log
stages.goal: Put daily traffic, sales, Buy Box share, ad spend and the dated changes into one dataset in this project, from the raw exports.

outputs.name: Dated timeline of changes and drop

checks.name: Units and ad spend totals in the dataset match the exports within 1%
At least three weeks before the drop and the three weeks of the drop are present, or the gap is stated
The reported 60 and 30 units a day are re-computed from the daily rows and the difference is stated

stages.name: Check the offer itself is healthy
stages.goal: Rule out the non-marketing causes first: lost Buy Box, price move, stock gap, listing suppressed, and ads or data that do not line up.

checks.name: Buy Box share is reported for every week; any week under 90% is flagged with the price and stock for that week
Ad-attributed orders are no more than total orders on any day, or the gap is explained
The listing is confirmed searchable for 'garlic press' (owner check) and not marked suppressed, or marked unchecked
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and what that means for the diagnosis

stages.name: Find what pushed the listing down
stages.goal: Split the drop into visits, buying rate and ad contribution, then test each hypothesis against the dated log. Keep competing explanations.

checks.name: Every hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN, with the numbers behind it
The change in units per day equals the sessions effect plus the unit session percentage effect, within 5%
Each main finding names at least one competing explanation
A cause is called SUPPORTED only if the step in the data begins within 3 days after the dated change

stages.name: Rank the fixes
stages.goal: Turn supported findings into a short ranked list of changes, each with expected effect, effort, confidence, risk, what it costs in ad spend and how it will be measured.

checks.name: Every option cites the finding it rests on
Every option has expected effect, effort, confidence, risk and how it will be measured
Every option keeps total Sponsored Products spend at or under $120 a day
Options are sequenced so only one listing change is live at a time

stages.name: Owner chooses
stages.goal: The owner picks the fixes and their order. Ask for the reason when they pass over the top option and record it.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over options are in decisions.jsonl
A reason is recorded wherever the top option was passed over

stages.name: Prepare the chosen fixes
stages.goal: Prepare only the chosen changes: image revert or test plan, listing copy, a reply to the 1-star review, and ad changes (search-term negatives, bids), each as exact steps the owner can apply in Seller Central.

outputs.name: Order of changes and test plan

checks.name: Only chosen changes are included
Every listing and image change is checked against Amazon's listing and image rules before the owner sees it
No search term is proposed as a negative with fewer than 20 clicks, unless the owner asked
Each change has the exact Seller Central place to make it and how to confirm it saved

stages.optional_when: No listing or ad change was chosen.

stages.name: Owner applies the changes one at a time
stages.goal: The owner applies each change on its planned date and logs it; register the test before the first change goes live. We never log in to Seller Central.

checks.name: Each test is registered in experiments.jsonl with its metric and read date before the change goes live
At least 7 days pass between listing changes, or the overlap is recorded
Every change has the date and time the owner made it

stages.name: Read the six weeks honestly
stages.goal: Each week, read units per day, sessions, unit session percentage, ad spend and search position against the target and the ceiling, and compare with the three weeks before the drop.

checks.name: Daily ad spend never above $120 and rating not below 4.4 are checked every week
Each change is compared with the 7 days before it and the same weekdays, using the same report definitions
A change is called a win only with at least 7 days of data after it; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE
Units per day come from the Seller Central report, not from our own estimate, and rank from the owner's logged-out search

stages.name: Keep what we learned
stages.goal: Close each test, record what moved units, and propose a weekly watch rule so the next slide is caught within a week.

checks.name: Every registered test is closed in experiments.jsonl
Each proposed rule says whether it holds for this listing, this business or the playbook

hypotheses.statement: The new main image lowered clicks or buying, which cut sales and then rank.
hypotheses.test: Compare sessions and unit session percentage for 14 days before and 14 days after the image change date, and Sponsored Products click-through rate on the same days.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Unit session percentage or ad click-through rate fell by 15% or more (relative) within 3 days of the change and has not recovered.
hypotheses.refute_if: Both stay within 5% of their earlier level for at least 7 days after the change.

hypotheses.statement: The 1-star review with photos lowered buying, and may point to a product problem.
hypotheses.test: Unit session percentage before and after the review date, rating trend, and whether other recent reviews repeat the complaint.
hypotheses.confirm_if: A step down of 10% or more (relative) in unit session percentage starts within 7 days of the review, and two or more other reviews repeat the complaint.
hypotheses.refute_if: No step at that date, or the drop began more than 14 days before the review.

hypotheses.statement: Ad spend is leaking or getting costlier, so it no longer supports sales and rank.
hypotheses.test: Cost per click, ad orders and wasted search terms (20 or more clicks, no orders) by week over the 12 weeks.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Cost per click rose 20% or more, or wasted terms take more than 25% of spend, while ad orders fell.
hypotheses.refute_if: Cost per click is within 10% and ad cost per order is steady.

hypotheses.statement: Price, Buy Box or stock changed and cut sales.
hypotheses.test: Weekly Buy Box share, price and stock for the garlic press against the drop.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Buy Box share fell below 90% in the weeks of the drop, or stock ran out for 2 or more days.
hypotheses.refute_if: Buy Box share stays above 95% and no stock gap.

hypotheses.statement: Fewer people reached the page (rank, competitors or season), not fewer bought.
hypotheses.test: Sessions per day against unit session percentage per day; owner's position checks.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Sessions fell 35% or more while unit session percentage moved less than 10%.
hypotheses.refute_if: Sessions are within 10% of before and the whole drop comes from unit session percentage.

hypotheses.statement: A rival moved above the listing with a lower price, a coupon or a better offer.
hypotheses.test: Owner's logged-out search: price, rating, review count and coupon badge of the top five results for 'garlic press' now, compared with the owner's notes from before.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Two or more rivals above the listing are cheaper by 10% or more or carry a deal badge, and unit session percentage fell.
hypotheses.refute_if: Top results are priced and badged as before.

measurement.window: Six weeks from approval, read weekly; compare each change with the 7 days before it and the same weekdays.
measurement.min_volume: At least 7 days of data after a change before it is called a win; fewer than that is INCONCLUSIVE.
measurement.stop_rule: Stop and ask the owner if daily Sponsored Products spend goes above $120, if rating falls below 4.4, or if units per day fall more than 15% below the level before the change.
